overall_summary: Bitcoin faces continued pressure after heavy liquidations and the worst ETF outflow week since June, while hotter jobs data lifts Fed hike odds and keeps the dollar firm. Regulatory bright spots like Coinbase’s OCC charter and Russia retail crypto access offer some support, but macro headwinds and fresh geopolitical energy disruptions dominate the near-term tone. Traders will watch Tuesday’s CPI and Fed speakers for the next catalyst.
key_points: ETF outflows hit $1.28B, worst since June
Jobs data lifts Fed hike odds, dollar firm
Coinbase wins full OCC national trust charter
Long liquidations exceed $1B after BTC drop
Geo energy hits and mixed Iran signals linger

items.title: BTC Crashes to $73.5K on Nvidia Probe, Iran Stall; $1B+ Longs Liquidated
items.summary: Bitcoin plunged to around seventy-three thousand five hundred dollars late Sunday, its lowest since August, after Nvidia's board opened a probe into CEO Jensen Huang over an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence and U.S.-Iran talks stalled. Thin weekend liquidity amplified the move, wiping out more than one billion dollars in leveraged positions, about nine hundred thirteen million of them longs, with ether hit even harder. Traders should care because this is a classic risk-off cascade that flushed leverage right before the Wall Street open, and the bounce back above seventy-four or seventy-five thousand is still fragile. Watch whether traditional markets and Nvidia reaction extend the selling or stabilize it.
items.impact: Near-term downside pressure and leverage flush; key supports under test

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $1.28B in Worst Week Since June
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw roughly one point two eight billion dollars in net outflows last week, the heaviest since late June, flipping twenty twenty-six year-to-date flows negative by about nine hundred fourteen million. BlackRock's IBIT dominated with around one point two one billion leaving, while Fidelity's FBTC managed modest inflows. This matters because ETF flows have been the main institutional on-ramp; sustained redemptions signal de-risking that can keep selling pressure on Bitcoin even after the weekend flush. Monday's flow print will show if the exodus is slowing.
items.impact: Continued institutional selling pressure on BTC price

items.title: Coinbase Wins Full OCC National Trust Charter
items.summary: Coinbase received full approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for its national trust bank charter, upgrading from conditional status granted in April. The Coinbase National Trust can now operate federally regulated digital-asset custody and payments services, though it still cannot take retail deposits or make loans. Traders should care because this deepens crypto's integration into the U.S. banking system, strengthens institutional custody options, and opens doors for stablecoin issuance under the GENIUS Act framework. It is a clear legitimacy win for the largest U.S. exchange amid broader regulatory noise.
items.impact: Positive for institutional adoption and Coinbase; supportive for crypto infrastructure

items.title: Senate Sets Jan. 4 Deadline for Binance, Tether, Trump Crypto Records
items.summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal, incoming chair of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations after the Democratic sweep, gave Binance, Tether, World Liberty Financial, and the TRUMP memecoin entity until January fourth to produce records or face alternative measures. The probes cover alleged illicit flows involving sanctioned entities and potential conflicts with Trump-linked firms. This creates fresh regulatory overhang just as Democrats take stronger control of Congress. Traders should watch for any compliance friction or headlines that could hit exchange volumes or stablecoin confidence.
items.impact: Regulatory overhang on major exchange and largest stablecoin

items.title: Binance Pool Mines Just One BTC Block Ahead of Shutdown
items.summary: Binance's Bitcoin mining pool found only one block in the past week, about zero point one one percent of network production, as its November tenth shutdown approaches. Hashrate has already collapsed from earlier levels near two percent of the network. The pool and related services end at seven UTC on the tenth, forcing remaining miners to migrate. This is minor for overall hashrate security but underscores Binance's retreat from mining infrastructure while it expands other products. Little direct price impact expected, though it removes one more pool from the landscape.
items.impact: Negligible for BTC price; minor hashrate redistribution

items.title: Bank of Russia Finalizes BTC, ETH, USDT for Retail Trading
items.summary: Russia's central bank has locked in Bitcoin, Ether, and USDT as the only assets non-qualified retail investors can buy under the new framework, effective November seventeenth, with a three hundred thousand ruble annual cap per intermediary. Qualified investors face no limits, and Moscow Exchange is preparing a December launch. This expands regulated access in a large market and gives Tether another official endorsement. For traders it is a modest long-term adoption positive, though the caps and tests limit immediate volume impact.
items.impact: Modest positive for regulated adoption and USDT utility

items.title: US CPI due Tuesday after hot jobs report
items.summary: October CPI drops tomorrow at 8:30 AM Eastern, with markets expecting about 0.3 percent month-over-month headline and core near 0.2 percent. The strong Friday jobs print already pushed December rate-hike odds near 80 percent, so a hot number would lock in more Fed tightening while a cool print could spark a relief rally in risk assets. Crypto traders should watch this closely because it will set the near-term path for yields, the dollar, and liquidity conditions.
items.impact: High volatility catalyst for rates, DXY, and BTC ahead of the print

items.title: October jobs surge lifts December Fed hike odds
items.summary: Nonfarm payrolls jumped 165,000 in October, more than double expectations, while unemployment fell to 4.1 percent. That strong reading reversed earlier doubts and lifted the market-implied chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the December 8-9 FOMC meeting to around 80-82 percent. Higher-for-longer rates tighten financial conditions, which typically pressures Bitcoin and other risk assets until the data path clarifies.
items.impact: Supports higher yields and dollar, headwind for crypto risk appetite

items.title: China PPI hits multi-year high, CPI cools
items.summary: China's October producer prices rose 5.7 percent year-over-year, the fastest in nearly four and a half years and above forecasts, driven by energy costs. Consumer prices eased to 0.7 percent year-over-year, below expectations, showing weak domestic demand. The split signal keeps global inflation pressures alive via commodities while highlighting China soft spots that could weigh on growth-sensitive assets.
items.impact: Mixed global inflation cue; energy pass-through vs demand weakness

items.title: Dollar holds firm near 102 on rate-hike bets
items.summary: The US Dollar Index stays supported above 101.8-102 after Friday's big gain on the jobs surprise, even as it eases slightly into Monday. Firm Treasury yields and elevated December hike pricing keep the greenback bid. A stronger dollar usually acts as a headwind for Bitcoin by tightening global dollar liquidity and pressuring risk assets.
items.impact: Dollar strength weighs on crypto and emerging-market risk

items.title: Treasury yields steady near 4.86 percent post-jobs
items.summary: The 10-year yield holds around 4.86 percent after rising on the strong payrolls data that reinforced Fed hike expectations. Front-end yields also firmed as markets priced more restrictive policy. Elevated real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and can slow speculative flows.
items.impact: Higher yields compete with crypto and tighten financial conditions

items.title: Fed speakers watched as hike path firms
items.summary: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee is scheduled today and other officials have recently backed gradual further tightening after the jobs beat. Comments from Daly and Barkin earlier reinforced that more rate increases are likely needed to cool still-elevated inflation. Any hawkish tilt this week will keep December odds elevated heading into CPI.
items.impact: Hawkish guidance sustains higher-rate pricing and risk-off pressure

items.title: Trump Signals Iran Strikes Unlikely as Oil Falls
items.summary: President Trump said fresh US attacks on Iran are highly unlikely if nuclear and Hormuz peace talks advance, with Qatar's PM set to meet him. Oil dropped further, Brent near 97 dollars, after last week's big decline, even as tanker incidents continue near the strait. Traders should watch this closely because de-escalation would ease energy prices and inflation pressure, supporting a risk-on move for Bitcoin and equities, while any breakdown could reverse it fast.
items.impact: Lower oil risk premium supports risk assets

items.title: Houthis Damage Aramco Tower in Riyadh Attack
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis launched missiles and drones at Riyadh, with debris damaging an Aramco administrative tower in the King Abdullah Financial District after Saudi intercepts. No casualties reported, but the group claimed hits on the financial center, airport and oil sites, prompting Saudi retaliation. This escalates the Saudi-Houthi front tied to the wider Iran conflict and keeps Gulf energy infrastructure at risk, which can spike oil volatility and hit risk sentiment.
items.impact: Heightens Gulf oil supply disruption fears

items.title: Drone Hit Halts Iraq Khor Mor Gas Field
items.summary: A suspected drone strike hit an LPG tank at the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan, suspending production and knocking out 2,500 to 2,800 megawatts of power. Over 70 percent of the region lost electricity with no injuries reported and no claim of responsibility. Energy shocks like this in a key producing area can lift gas and oil prices regionally and add to broader Middle East risk that pressures crypto and risk assets.
items.impact: Regional energy blackout and supply risk premium

items.title: Russia Strikes Ukraine Grid Ahead of Abu Dhabi Talks
items.summary: Russian missile and drone barrages hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure, leaving hundreds of thousands without power and forcing Zaporizhzhia plant onto generators. Trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine talks are set for Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, with Europeans now joining. Persistent winter energy attacks raise the stakes for any ceasefire progress; success could ease global risk, while failure keeps safe-haven flows and volatility elevated for markets.
items.impact: Talks outcome will drive near-term risk sentiment

items.title: Democrats' Congress Win Pressures Iran War and Tariffs
items.summary: After the Democratic sweep of both chambers, lawmakers signal plans to use oversight and legislation to push ending the Iran war and rolling back tariffs. Trump has linked the war to midterm losses and is floating deals, while G7 foreign ministers meet amid the shift. Reduced war funding risk and potential tariff relief could lower inflation and support risk assets, though gridlock and investigations add uncertainty.
items.impact: Policy shift may ease war and trade headwinds

items.title: Eisenkot Tapped to Form Israeli Government
items.summary: Israeli President Herzog tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming a coalition after inconclusive elections left no majority. This follows Netanyahu's weakened position amid the Iran war and regional fighting. A new government could alter Israel's approach to Iran, Gaza and alliances, creating near-term uncertainty for Middle East risk premiums that affect oil and broader markets.
items.impact: Coalition outcome may shift regional security stance
